metadata.title: AI Concerns Resurface? ORCL, GOOGL, SPCX, CRWV Credit Default Swap Spreads Hit Records As NVDA, ANT Tumble

content.text:
AI Concerns Resurface? ORCL, GOOGL, SPCX, CRWV Credit Default Swap Spreads Hit Records As NVDA, ANT Tumble
-
Five-year credit default swap (CDS) spreads at Oracle, Alphabet, SpaceX, and CoreWeave hit record levels, according to S&P.
-
CoreWeave's bonds dropped sharply on Tuesday.
-
Retail sentiment was 'bullish' for NVDA and QQQ, 'bearish' for ORCL and GOOGL, 'neutral' for CRWV, and 'extremely bullish' for ANT.
Tech stocks renewed their selloff on Tuesday and derivatives betting on credit default surged, signaling a declining sentiment in the AI market.
The Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 (QQQ), which tracks tech stocks, declined 1.2% in overnight trading, while AI bellwether stocks Nvidia (NVDA) and Anthropic (ANT) shed 2% and 2.3%, respectively. The moves follow a broad tech rally on Monday after Nvidia rehired Jensen Huang as CEO with immediate effect.
Overnight, five-year credit default swap (CDS) spreads at Oracle (ORCL), Alphabet (GOOGL), SpaceX (SPCX) and CoreWeave (CRWV) hit record levels, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence figures reported by Reuters, pushing data center operator CoreWeave's default probability in the next five years to 68%.
CDS are financial contracts that act like insurance against a borrower defaulting on its debt, compensating the buyer if the borrower fails to repay. The wider their spread, the greater the perceived risk of default.
Meanwhile, CoreWeave's 9% bond due in 2031 dropped as much as 3.6 points to 76.6 cents on the dollar, the lowest since it was issued in July 2025, according to Trace data reported by Bloomberg.
Its 9.75% note due in 2031 sank 3.75 points to hit 76.3 cents, a low since issuance in April. And its 9.25% bond due 2030 slid 3 points to 80.9 cents, its lowest since it was issued in May 2025.
Shares of SoftBank, which has investments in several AI and chip companies, fell over 14% in Tokyo on Wednesday.
Market Reviews Tech Positions
Together, the markers point to renewed concerns around the durability of the AI trade, which weighed tech stocks in October as well.
Investors are still forming a view on a series of market-moving events that have kept tech stocks on edge of late.
Huang's return as Nvidia CEO, the continued slide in Anthropic shares after a strong debut last Thursday, and Democrats' midterm election win have each added a new dimension, leaving investors to reassess both the opportunities and risks surrounding the sector.
While Huang's return has raised expectations of a renewed push into AI, it has also brought competitive concerns for companies such as Anthropic.
